title: ScopedTracked
hints: Where must `delete p_` go so that it runs however the scope ends: fall-through, early `return`, `break`, or an exception? There is exactly one member function the compiler calls for you at the closing brace.

`~ScopedTracked() { delete p_; }`. Because `delete nullptr` is a no-op, `release()` only has to hand the pointer out and set `p_ = nullptr`; the destructor then has nothing left to do. Forbid copying with `= delete` on the copy constructor and copy assignment, or two wrappers end up deleting the same object.
